During the 1971 India-Pakistan war (also known as the Bangladesh Liberation War), Richard Nixon was the President of the United States [d2][d3][d4]. Nixon covertly aided Pakistan during the conflict, and he and National Security Adviser Henry Kissinger broke the American arms ban on Pakistan to ensure Islamabad received air support from third countries like Jordan [d4]. On the Pakistani side, Yahya Khan was the President of Pakistan at the time, described as the "last President of a united Pakistan" [d2][d1]. There was also a notable meeting between Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and President Nixon in November 1971, where she rejected US advice against intervening in the conflict [d6]. Nixon and Kissinger spent long hours during the war discussing how to "scare off the Indians" by encouraging China to threaten India, reflecting Nixon's pro-Pakistan stance [d5].
